objective: Make verified Quest v2 objective progress, completion, and canonical reward commit atomically through one idempotent controller action, eliminating completed-without-reward partial state while preserving all existing actions and player-state authority.

roles_before.artifact: All System writes pass through PostgreSQL system_apply_action or the behaviorally matched memory store.
quest.complete appends a completion after required Quest v2 objectives are already complete.
progression.award is a separate verified write linked to a completion and checked against system-quest-reward:v1.
Each action has one request hash and Idempotency-Key conflict boundary.
system_events is append-only and Neon remains the sole mutable owner of derived RPG state.
Existing quest.progress, quest.complete and progression.award actions remain available for compatibility and diagnostics.
A code deployment cannot itself create progress, completion, reward, profile, or other player events.
Previous completion and award behavior remains recoverable from Git/deployment rollback.

role_dispositions.destination: Additive system_resolve_quest_v1 database gate is invoked by the same store/API boundary and composes existing validated child actions inside one transaction.
The canonical quest.completed event and all objective/terminal validation remain unchanged.
The canonical progression.awarded event, verified evidence requirement, one-award constraint, and calibrated reward check remain unchanged.
quest.resolve derives stable child keys from one root key and anchors the full request hash on completion so exact retries replay and changed reuse conflicts.
Only ordinary validated child events are appended; no update/delete or second state owner is introduced.
All existing action types and HTTP response fields remain supported; quest.resolve is additive.
Migration and deployment create only code/functions; production verification is read-only and player events require a later authorized action call.
Base code and schema are retained in Git history; the new function is additive and callers can continue using legacy actions.

capability_probes.assertion: quest.progress, quest.complete and progression.award retain their existing validation and response behavior.
If required objectives or canonical reward validation fails, no progress, completion, or reward child event survives.
Profile calibration, shop, deadline expiry, push delivery, PWA session, and legacy LifeUp regressions still pass.
The exact base SHA retains the previous separate action flow and all production data remains compatible.

tests.expected: Verified resolve appends progress, completion and exact reward; exact retry replays; invalid completion leaves no partial events.
PostgreSQL transaction and concurrent/idempotent gate prove all-or-nothing completion plus reward.

verification.production_player_mutation: FORBIDDEN — this slice deploys only additive code/function behavior and performs read-only production verification.
